title: Sky Aglow at CTIO
caption: Zodiacal light and airglow over the Blanco 4-meter Telescope, Cerro Tololo
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A dim white gleam rises vertically on the left side of this photograph. On the right, beside the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope at NSF NOIRLab's Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO), bands of colored light lie along the horizon. Two different effects light up this night sky.

The white gleam is zodiacal light, which is sunlight scattered by dust drifting between the planets of our Solar System. The light starts at the Sun and reaches us only after bouncing off those tiny grains.

The colored bands are airglow, and they begin much closer to home, in Earth's own atmosphere. Gases high in the atmosphere give off a faint light of their own at night, and here that light tints the sky close to the horizon.

understand.summary: A night-sky landscape photograph by B. Tafreshi. No camera or exposure details or color mapping are published.
understand.eye: Both zodiacal light and airglow are faint, and a long camera exposure gathers far more of their light than the eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The credit names the photographer as B. Tafreshi. NOIRLab released the photograph as an Image of the Week under the title "Sky Aglow at CTIO". Of the two glows it shows, only airglow comes from Earth itself.
alt: A dim white vertical glow on the left of a night sky and colored bands along the horizon to the right of the Blanco telescope.
